subtopic: RESTful Resource Modeling and HTTP Semantics
question_text: When designing a REST API, what is the semantic difference between `PUT` and `PATCH`?

options.text: PUT is for creation only; PATCH is for deletion
PUT replaces the entire resource representation; PATCH applies partial modifications to specific fields
PATCH is guaranteed idempotent; PUT is never idempotent
PUT requires SSL; PATCH does not

answer_explanation: PUT semantically replaces the complete target resource. Any omitted fields in a PUT payload are cleared or defaulted. PATCH applies partial deltas to modify only specified fields.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: PUT semantically replaces the complete target resource. Any omitted fields in a PUT payload are cleared or defaulted. PATCH applies partial deltas to modify only specified fields.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
